business_scope.primary_industry_name: Zinc Alloy Die-Casting and Tampo Printing of 1:18 Scale Car Replicas

stage_1.expense_line_item: Notarial certification of the incorporation deed and Articles of Association (Statuten)
stage_1.charging_authority: Cantonal public notary (Canton of Zug or Zurich)
stage_1.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff; typical CHF 300–800 for standard AG incorporation deed

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations, OR/CO), Arts. 626-763 (Aktiengesellschaft); incorporation procedure Arts. 629-640; registered office Art. 716; commercial register filing Arts. 641 and 938-951; name law Arts. 944-948; audit provisions Arts. 727-731a; implementing Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) of the canton of registered office, under federal supervision of the Federal Department of Justice and Police; electronic submission via e.chregister and public name search via Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Anmeldung (registration application) accompanied by the notarized deed of incorporation (öffentliche Urkunde) and the Articles of Association (Statuten)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000; at least 20% (minimum CHF 50,000) must be paid up in cash and deposited into a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss bank before registration; the bank's escrow confirmation must evidence that the funds remain at the company's free disposal for the post-registration operational period
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the organizational meeting held on [date] at the registered office, the Board unanimously resolved: 1. Share Subscription: Ratified; the entire share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 nominal value each, is fully subscribed and allotted, and the bank escrow deposit of CHF 50,000 is acknowledged. 2. Registered Office: The registered office is established at [street], [canton], Switzerland. 3. Officers: [Name] is appointed Chairman, [Name] and [Name] are appointed Board members, and [Name] is appointed Managing Director with individual signature authority. All officers are authorized to file the company with the Commercial Register and complete all formation formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zefix central business index and the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a registered-name search on Zefix for the proposed corporate names; verify compliance with Swiss name law (Art. 944-948 OR), including absence of misleading elements and inclusion of the corporate identifier 'AG'. Where the canton offers optional name reservation, file a reservation application; otherwise confirm availability on the register before drafting the articles of association.
required_dossiers: Zefix name search protocol
List of three proposed corporate names in ranked order
Passport or ID copies of founding shareholders for AML verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a conflicting or identical name is retrieved, re-file using the alternate proposed names or obtain a written waiver or consent from the owner of the prior similar name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal notary public (Notariat) in the canton of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the deed of incorporation before a licensed Swiss notary who attests the identity, legal capacity, and signatures of all founders. The notarized Articles of Association must state the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose (manufacture of zinc-alloy die-cast scale automotive models), share capital, share categories, board composition, audit rules and official communication method. The notary certifies the founders' signatures and transmits the filing dossier to the Commercial Register or provides e.chregister submission credentials.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association signed by all founders
Valid passports or Swiss residence permits of all founders
Founders' declarations of acceptance of board and audit mandates
Power of attorney if any founder is legally represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects such as missing mandatory clauses, an invalid corporate name, or an uncured capital statement, revise the draft and re-execute the deed in a supplementary notarial instrument without restarting the incorporation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Blocked Escrow Account and Obtaining Bank Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank (cantonal bank or FINMA-licensed private bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company 'in formation' at a Swiss bank; deposit at least CHF 50,000 (20% of the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital) by wire transfer from the founders' personal accounts. Instruct the bank to issue a bank confirmation (Bankbestätigung) addressed to the Commercial Register certifying that the required amount is credited and remains blocked and irrevocably at the company's disposal until registration is effected.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation (certified excerpt)
AML and CDB forms for the company in formation
Identification documents and UBO declarations of all founding shareholders
Board resolution on the escrow account mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the relationship or issues an incomplete confirmation, approach another licensed Swiss bank and resubmit the AML documentation; the confirmation may be reissued after depositing the capital in the required currency (CHF) and repositioning the funds in the blocked account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Statutory Auditor or Small-Company Opt-Out Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and, where applicable, the Federal Audit Oversight Authority (FAOA / RAAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: An Aktiengesellschaft must appoint an auditor under Art. 727 OR unless the shareholders validly declare the small-company opt-out under Art. 727a OR (fewer than ten full-time employees and balance-sheet or turnover thresholds not exceeded). Secure the signed acceptance of a licensed Swiss audit firm, or prepare the shareholders' unanimous opt-out written declaration together with the board resolution confirming that the statutory exemption criteria are met.
required_dossiers: Audit firm engagement and acceptance letter
Shareholders' opt-out declaration if the audit is waived
Board resolution ratifying the auditor election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If no licensed auditor accepts the mandate, engage an alternative FINMA-supervised audit firm or licensed Swiss fiduciary (Treuhänder); if the opt-out is challenged, retroactively appoint an auditor at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Entry in the Swiss Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via e.chregister
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration application (Anmeldung) electronically or in writing, attaching the notarized deed of incorporation, the bank escrow confirmation, the specimen signatures of the Chairman, Board members and Managing Director, and the auditor acceptance or opt-out declaration. The registrar reviews the filing for statutory compliance, effects the entry in the Commercial Register and publishes the incorporation; the company acquires legal personality upon entry, evidenced by an official extract (Handelsregisterauszug).
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and certified Articles of Association
Bank confirmation of the blocked capital deposit
Certified specimen signature cards of all authorized signatories
Auditor acceptance letter or opt-out declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a deficiency notice (Frist zur Behebung von Mängeln) is issued, cure the stated defects within the registry-set deadline, commonly 20 to 30 days, by filing the missing documents; changes to the articles triggered by the cure must be certified by a notary before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Company Identification Number, VAT and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFC), cantonal tax authority, AHV/IV/EO compensation office (Ausgleichskasse) and SUVA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Commercial Register entry automatically notifies the Federal Tax Administration, which issues the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer). The company must separately register for VAT if annual worldwide turnover is expected to exceed CHF 100,000, register employees with the cantonal compensation office for AHV/IV/EO social insurance, enroll with SUVA for occupational accident insurance, and file the cantonal corporate income and capital tax registration with the competent cantonal tax office.
required_dossiers: Official Commercial Register extract
UID allocation notice from ESTV
Identification documents of directors and managing director
Lease agreements and industrial premises address
Projected turnover and employee count declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID notification or tax registration is delayed, apply directly to ESTV using Form UID and attach the Commercial Register extract; late registration may be regularized by requesting administrative leniency and paying any minimal late-filing surcharge assessed by the tax authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Labor Inspectorate (Arbeitsinspektorat), Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA) for occupational health, and the cantonal building authority (Bauinspektorat) for the industrial premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial establishment operating permit (gewerbliche Betriebsbewilligung) and building-use permit for the zinc die-casting foundry and tampo-printing production line

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU) acting through the competent cantonal environmental protection office (kantonale Umweltschutzfachstelle)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EIA screening and preliminary examination (Vorprüfung) under Annex 1, item 71.1 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV / EIE): low-capacity zinc die-casting plant classified below the mandatory full-report threshold and rated as environmental compliance registration; where furnace thermal input, production capacity or hazardous waste volumes exceed applicable thresholds, the classification is upgraded to a full EIA report
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limits for zinc, copper, nickel and total suspended solids under the Swiss Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV); air emission limits for PM10, metal particulates, zinc oxide fumes and VOC abatement from tampo-printing inks under the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV); hazardous solid residues and die-cast slag handling, storage and disposal per the Waste Ordinance (VVEA)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the cantonal fire protection authority (Feuerpolizei / Gebäudeversicherung) covering casting furnaces, drying ovens and solvent storage; structural load inspection certificate for the heavy die-cast machine foundations; SUVA occupational safety clearance for hot-metal handling, machine guard interlocks, and workplace ventilation systems

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), VAT Main Division (Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer), Berne; cantonal and communal tax administrations of the AG's registered seat; Swiss Customs Administration (Oberzolldirektion). Official portals: https://www.estv.admin.ch, eTaxOnWeb (electronic filing), https://www.uid.admin.ch (UID register), https://www.zefix.ch (Central Business Register).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – Incorporate the AG: notarize the articles of association (minimum share capital CHF 100,000, of which CHF 50,000 must be fully paid in), obtain the bank capital-confirmation certificate, and file for entry in the Commercial Register of the canton of seat. The Commercial Register transmits the entry to the Swiss Central Business Register (ZEFIX), which automatically assigns the Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer (UID, format CHE-123.456.789) under the Federal Act on the Business Identification Number (UIDG). Step 2 – VAT/TIN registration: the Swiss-resident AG applies electronically via eTaxOnWeb to the ESTV VAT Main Division for inclusion in the VAT register; the UID then serves as the statutory VAT identification number (MWST-Nr / TVA-No) under Art. 110 MWSTG. Registration is mandatory without delay once annual taxable turnover in Switzerland exceeds CHF 100,000; voluntary registration is available below this threshold and confers the right to deduct input VAT. A foreign entity without a Swiss seat or permanent establishment uses the simplified registration form and must appoint a tax representative domiciled in Switzerland; its MWST-Nr is likewise derived from its UID or a provisional VAT number. Step 3 – Profit-tax registration: upon incorporation, the cantonal tax administration of the registered seat opens the corporate tax file (cantonal and communal profit and equity taxes) and the ESTV opens the Direct Federal Tax file; all filings reference the UID. Step 4 – Obtain a certified UID/VAT extract from the UID register portal for banking onboarding (SWIFT), PayPal integration and counterparty validation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – the Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG) is a resident corporate taxpayer with unlimited tax liability on worldwide income for Direct Federal Tax (8.5% of net profit) and cantonal/communal profit tax plus an annual equity tax (Kapitalsteuer). No pass-through regime, no territorial system and no tax-exempt zone applies to a manufacturing AG in Switzerland.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law provides no check-the-box classification and no general hybrid-mismatch election; OECD hybrid mismatch outcomes are neutralized by mandatory anti-hybrid, CFC and interest-barrier rules. Genuine statutory elections available: (1) small-enterprise VAT option under Art. 11 MWSTG for taxable turnover below CHF 100,000, binding for at least five years; (2) VAT group taxation under Art. 13 MWSTG for closely linked enterprises (substantial financial, economic and organizational intertwining), binding for at least five years; (3) partial taxation of dividends from qualified participations (deemed 70% exemption) for individual shareholders; (4) cantonal patent-box and additional notional-interest-deduction election for self-developed qualifying IP under the Swiss Tax Reform Act 2020 (STAF); (5) customs AEO (Authorized Economic Operator) certification; and (6) for foreign-parented groups, the mandatory Swiss branch profit-tax and deemed-liquidation exit rules (non-elective).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA) levied under the Swiss Federal Act on Value Added Tax (MWSTG / LTVA), administered by the ESTV VAT Main Division.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual taxable turnover from Swiss supplies (including zero-rated exports; excluding exempt supplies) under Art. 10 para. 2 lit. c and Art. 110 MWSTG. Foreign suppliers of electronic or digital services to Swiss consumers are mandatorily registrable from the first franc under Art. 18b MWSTG. Domestic small businesses may voluntarily register from the first franc.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no statutory e-invoicing mandate, no API clearance portal and no digital stamping exist under Swiss VAT law as of 2025. The Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) has been the mandatory standardized payment slip for all invoices payable in Switzerland since 1 July 2020, embedding the QR-IBAN, creditor data and UID/VAT metadata. Electronic invoices are voluntarily exchanged in standard formats (UBL 2.0 Swiss extension, Factur-X/ZUGFeRD, PDF/XML bundles); no authorization or clearance request is submitted to the tax authority before issuance. VAT returns are filed electronically through the ESTV eTaxOnWeb/ELM portal. Invoices, customs export declarations and transport documents must be retained in a traceable, chronologically complete archive for ten years (Art. 58 para. 4 MWSTG).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports under Art. 23 para. 1 lit. 1 MWSTG: the supply is zero-rated if (i) the die-cast products are physically transported from Swiss customs territory into a foreign customs territory; (ii) delivery occurs to the foreign purchaser or to a third party commissioned by the purchaser abroad; and (iii) the supplier substantiates the export through the Swiss customs export declaration (e-dec/PASSAR output, or CN22/CN23 postal customs declaration for parcel shipments) and an international transport document (CMR consignment note, bill of lading, sea/air waybill). Export sales through Swiss freight forwarders are zero-rated only where the supplier obtains an export certificate from the customs-clearing forwarder. Related offshore services: work performed on movable property in Switzerland (e.g., custom tampo printing, painting, assembly or repair of scale replicas) followed by export of the goods is zero-rated under Art. 23 para. 1 lit. 4 MWSTG. Pure services supplied to a business customer domiciled abroad whose place of supply lies abroad under Art. 18 MWSTG are not subject to Swiss VAT and are invoiced at 0% with a statutory place-of-supply reference. All export substantiation must be archived for ten years and presented to the ESTV on request.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss customs export declaration accepted by Swiss Customs (e-dec/PASSAR output, or CN22/CN23 postal customs declaration) identifying the AG as exporter and stating goods description, value, destination and the exporter's UID/VAT number
International transport document evidencing physical departure: original bill of lading, sea/air waybill, or CMR consignment note signed by the consignee or forwarder abroad
Commercial invoice, packing list and, where applicable, the Swiss Federal Customs Administration export certificate for consignments cleared by a third-party freight forwarder

Payment substantiation: SWIFT MT103/MT202 credit advice or PayPal settlement/payout report, together with carrier delivery confirmation and acknowledgement from the foreign buyer (Switzerland imposes no fixed foreign-currency repatriation deadline; export proceeds may be held abroad and settled in EUR, USD or CHF)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are screened by the ESTV against Swiss customs exit records (PASSAR data matching) and are priority targets in VAT audits of e-commerce collectibles sellers. If the exporter cannot substantiate physical departure of the goods, the supply is retroactively reclassified as domestically taxable at 8.1% (standard rate), the corresponding input VAT credits are refused or clawed back, and the underpaid VAT is assessed with statutory default interest within the general 5-year limitation period (Art. 84 para. 1 MWSTG), extended to ten years in cases of qualified tax fraud (Art. 84 para. 3 MWSTG). Culpable failure to document exports or intentional misdeclaration constitutes tax evasion under Arts. 176–178 MWSTG, carrying fines of up to three times the tax evaded; qualified tax fraud under Art. 186 MWSTG read with the Federal Administrative Criminal Law (VStrR) is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years or a monetary penalty, with the evaded tax also due. Forged customs declarations, bills of lading or delivery receipts additionally trigger prosecution under Art. 251 of the Swiss Criminal Code (forgery of documents) and independent penalties under the Swiss Customs Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB / Schweizerische Nationalbank) acting under the National Bank Act and Art. 99 of the Federal Constitution, in conjunction with the Federal Department of Finance (FDF) and the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF). Switzerland maintains no standalone foreign-exchange administration; the SNB is responsible for monetary policy, the SIC/EuroSIC payment systems, and banknote issuance, while the Federal Council holds dormant emergency powers under the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (WZG).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible on both current and capital account; Swiss law imposes no exchange-control permit, prior-authorization regime, or repatriation approval for inbound equity, outbound dividends, intercompany loans, or trade settlements. Profit remittance by the CH_AG is unrestricted and executed freely via SIC/EuroSIC/SEPA/SWIFT, subject only to the Swiss federal withholding tax of 35% on dividend distributions (Verrechnungssteuer), which is refundable or reduced under double-taxation treaties or Swiss participation-relief rules. No circular-transaction clearance or currency-approval document is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland has no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation for export proceeds. The die-cast model exporter may retain CHF, EUR, USD, or CNY receivables domestically or abroad, may adopt internal treasury netting, and may determine FX conversion purely by corporate treasury policy without notifying the SNB or SIF.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto per CO Art. 633) plus primary operational account
Operational Account (payables/disbursement desk, SIC and SWIFT MT103)
Operational Account (Zug commercial substance and cantonal identity)
EUR-denominated Operational Account for EU trade payables

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low as primary treasury but viable as ancillary rails. EU/UK EMIs cannot passport an EMI licence into Switzerland; Art. 1b of the Banking Act restricts Swiss fintech operations to licensed domestic players such as Alpian, Yuh, and Bank Cler, while foreign EMIs may only provide card-issuing or collection-aggregation services through Swiss partner banks. The statutory capital escrow account and the main treasury must remain with a fully licensed Swiss bank to establish commercial substance under CO Art. 633 and to satisfy bank assurance obligations imposed by FINMA Circular 2020/01.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in practice. Under the VSB 20 due-diligence standards and FINMA Circular 2020/01, non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners of the CH_AG must generally attend an in-person KYC interview at a Swiss bank branch or before a Swiss notary completing the Form A beneficial-owner verification. Remote onboarding via FINMA-recognised video identification is admissible only for low-risk profiles and at the bank's absolute discretion; the PayPal micro-transaction income complicates that classification, so at least one authorized director or a Swiss-resident attorney-in-fact registered in the commercial register should appear physically in Zug.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident sole shareholder with no prior Swiss banking relationship and no Swiss tax identification number
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport, power-of-attorney, source-of-wealth statement, audited financial statements of the parent, board resolution on the CH_AG's commercial plan, Swiss office lease agreement in Zug, and a commercial-register excerpt confirming the paid-up capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume PayPal marketplace receivables inconsistent with a physical-goods manufacturer, raising transaction-pattern alerts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Marketplace settlement reports, collector-store merchant statements, refund and chargeback policy, ERP order-to-cash reconciliation, warehouse and logistics contracts, and a 24-month rolling cash-flow forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large outbound disbursements to China and Hong Kong tooling and zinc-alloy suppliers before revenue history exists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders, proforma invoices and bills of lading, Incoterms 2020 contracts, an arm's-length pricing memorandum supporting customs value, supplier beneficial-ownership declarations, and confirmation that no shipment is dual-use or embargoed under SECO export-control and Swiss sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structural ambiguity between the initial capital escrow deposit and subsequent shareholder loans, risking hidden capital contribution re-characterisation under CO Art. 678
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital-increase resolution, bank confirmation of the Sperrkonto release, a formal subordination letter for shareholder loans, and tax-recognition memoranda distinguishing equity from debt to prevent unintended dividend treatment or stamp-duty exposure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 from the parent or contributing shareholder to the CH_AG's Swiss bank with field 72/77B explicitly labelled 'Kapitaleinlage gem. Verwaltungsratsbeschluss / Non-repayable capital contribution'; the credit clears through SIC for CHF or EuroSIC/SEPA for EUR. Switzerland operates no statutory purpose-code system, so the remittance narrative must align with the commercial-register capital confirmation and the board minutes required under CO Art. 633. Contributions exceeding the registered share capital are posted to capital reserves with a Zug cantonal tax-office confirmation for stamp-duty review under the Federal Act on Stamp Duties; no prior SNB notification is required, but the receiving bank applies enhanced due diligence for amounts above CHF 50,000 originating from non-OECD jurisdictions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for zinc alloy, tampo printing inks, and acrylic display packaging are executed via SWIFT MT103 single-payment messages over SIC/EuroSIC for CHF/EUR and via USD correspondent banking for USD payables; Chinese tooling and Hong Kong settlement flows are structured through irrevocable documentary letters of credit (MT700, UCP 600) or MT103 with Incoterms 2020 compliance; PayPal collection balances are automatically swept daily to the Swiss operational account through the bank's payment aggregator link, eliminating PSP settlement risk and preserving an auditable trail for VAT and corporate income-tax accruals.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards on CHF/EUR, CHF/USD, and EUR/CHF under the Swiss Bankers Association short-form FX master agreement
Cross-currency swaps on CHF/EUR and CHF/USD for longer-dated balance-sheet hedging under ISDA 2002
Non-deliverable forwards on CNH/CNY to hedge Chinese yuan tooling payables without onshore permit requirements
FX options and zero-cost collars on EUR/USD and CHF/EUR booked with the relationship bank
Forward overlay on USD-denominated PayPal collections to reduce conversion spread leakage in monthly sweeps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' meeting and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register (minutes retained by the AG; filings restricted to capital and officer changes; standard annual accounts are not filed with the register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after balance sheet date; for a 31-December year-end, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct administrative strike-off; repeated failure to convene the general meeting exposes the board to personal liability and permits creditors to petition the court for remedial measures or, in extreme cases, involuntary liquidation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cantonal and federal corporate income tax return with net wealth tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Office of the registered office and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing generally no later than 6 to 9 months after fiscal year-end; cantons may grant extensions; federal direct tax assessment follows the cantonal tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 4%–5% p.a. and preventive fines typically CHF 200–5,000 per canton; failure to file permits tax-derived assessment and debt enforcement; Swiss law does not impose commercial-register strike-off for tax delinquency, but unpaid taxes may culminate in forced liquidation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT return (quarterly or annual method)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration, VAT Main Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly returns due within 60 days after end of each quarter; annual-return method due by 30 June of the subsequent year if permitted by the FTA for smaller taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 5% p.a.; fines up to three times the evaded tax for intentional VAT evasion; repeated non-filing may trigger criminal prosecution but not automatic commercial-register strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual review and confirmation of UBO records and shareholder register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors (records retained with the AG's statutory registers; no central UBO filing is made under Swiss law)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Register updated contemporaneously upon each transfer of shares and confirmed at the annual general meeting, normally by 30 June for calendar-year accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML administrative fines up to CHF 500,000 for record-keeping breaches; unregistered transferees lose voting rights and dividend claims; if a registered shareholder fails to provide beneficial-owner details, voting rights are suspended; long-term administrative non-existence of a registered office can result in liquidation by the commercial register authority

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) audit is compulsory for an AG exceeding for two consecutive years any two of: balance sheet total CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, 250 FTE employees; listed companies, companies subject to supervisory regulation, and certain group companies also require a full audit. Other AGs are subject to a limited audit unless all shareholders approve an opt-out and the AG has fewer than 10 FTE employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting provisions; Swiss GAAP FER for SMGs and larger AGs; IFRS is permitted for statutory accounts and mandatory for listed companies; real-estate holding AGs must provide specific additional schedules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Swiss AML rules the AG must identify and record the beneficial owner of every shareholder, nominee, or legal entity before a share transfer is recognised. The register is updated at transfer and reviewed at the annual general meeting; bearer shareholders may only exercise voting rights after disclosing their beneficial owner. No central UBO filing exists under Swiss law; the annual confirmation protocol is a board-level certification supported by minutes and signed declarations.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–1,800 per year for a commercial registered office or fiduciario in Zug or a major canton, including register support and AGM administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–12,000 for a limited statutory audit; USD 12,000–25,000 for a full statutory audit of a mid-sized die-cast manufacturer

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal statutory corporate income tax (calculated on profit after federal tax; pre-tax equivalent 7.83%; plus varying cantonal/communal corporate income tax, producing aggregate headline rates of approximately 14.6%–24.4% depending on canton/municipality).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No federal tax holidays; preferential measures include patent box/qualifying IP deduction (up to 90% exemption), mandatory R&D superdeduction (additional deduction of up to 50% of qualifying R&D personnel and other costs), participation relief (dividends and capital gains on qualifying 10%+ holdings are generally tax-exempt), and notional interest deduction on excess Swiss equity; cantonal tax relief are additional and vary by seat.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined Swiss federal and cantonal corporate income tax return for legal entities ('Steuererklärung juristische Personen' / 'Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales'), submitted electronically through the competent cantonal tax authority's e-portal (eTax/electronic filing software used by the canton; federal direct tax is assessed within the same return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayments of expected corporate tax are required, but the formal return is filed once per fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due within 6-9 months after the balance-sheet date; calendar-year AGs in most cantons must file by 31 May or 30 June of the following year. A written extension may postpone filing to 30 September or beyond, but no later than the assessment notice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Commercial Register UID/CH number, registered seat, fiscal-year closing date, and name/address of the auditor or fiduciary preparing the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert only the Swiss AG's registered details; non-resident shareholders are not listed on this line, but a shareholder register showing holdings and residence must be attached for withholding tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover, cost of sales, distribution costs, R&D expense, depreciation, and net operating profit from the die-cast automotive replica business; must reconcile to audited IFRS/OR financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income booked in Switzerland; if a foreign permanent establishment exists in the parent or a third country, allocate the PE profit separately and avoid double-counting intercompany sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses added back (excessive director remuneration, fines, political contributions, bribes); deduct IP-box income, R&D superdeduction, notional interest deduction, and participation relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees or royalties paid to non-resident parent must be expressly disclosed, have valid agreements, and satisfy arm's-length tests; undocumented deductions are denied and may be recharacterized as dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 130 / Taxable Profit and Tax Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net profit before deductions, statutory additions/reductions, taxable profit after deductions, federal tax base, cantonal/communal tax base, and final corporate tax amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned Swiss AG, federal and cantonal taxable profit are computed at entity level; no foreign tax credit for the shareholder is claimed in this return, and dividend distribution has no impact on taxable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 200 / Equity and Capital Tax Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Paid-in share capital, capital contribution reserves, statutory reserves, other free reserves, retained earnings, and distributable profit; used for cantonal capital tax and for assessing WHT on later distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full amount of paid-up capital and taxed reserves available for distribution; the company must file a separate Verrechnungssteuer declaration for each dividend paid to foreign shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers default assessment, procedural fines (typically CHF 100-5,000), interest on late tax, and, for intentionally incorrect returns, criminal tax-evasion penalties of up to 100%-300% of the under-assessed tax; repeated non-compliance can lead to statutory strike-off and director liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends paid by an AG; final/relief under double tax agreements may reduce the rate to 0-15% depending on shareholding and treaty partner, with 0-5% for qualifying parent-subsidiary holdings under many Swiss DTAs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss AG withholds and remits 35% to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA). The non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain a valid tax-residence certificate (TRC) from the competent authority of the treaty state; (2) file a refund / reduced-withholding application with the FTA on the prescribed form within three years from the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became due; (3) attach dividend vouchers, documentary evidence of shareholding percentage and holding period, and a beneficial-owner statement; (4) obtain FTA approval for refund or for future reduced rate where the applicable DTA allows.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: No Swiss statutory withholding tax is imposed on outbound royalties, but royalties paid to a related non-resident must be arm's length, otherwise the excess may be recharacterized as constructive dividends subject to 35% WHT. Swiss statutory withholding tax (35%) applies to interest on Swiss public bonds and money-market instruments; ordinary bank interest and interest on non-public related-party loans are generally not subject to Swiss WHT. Under Swiss DTAs, outbound interest is commonly reduced to 0-10% and outbound royalties to 0-10% (often 0% for license fees).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: Swiss AG engaged in cross-border related-party transactions above CHF 1,000,000 in aggregate per fiscal year is expected to maintain arm's-length documentation in the form required by the Swiss FTA/OECD TP Manual; Master File and Country-by-Country Report: mandatory for ultimate parent groups with consolidated revenue of CHF 900,000,000 or more. Documentation must be produced to the tax assessor on request in German/French/Italian or in translated/English form.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime; however, the General Anti-Abuse Rule and Federal Supreme Court practice require an AG to have real economic substance in Switzerland (business premises, competent staff, actual management decisions, bank account and commercial activity). A 'letter-box' company invoking treaty benefits and profit attribution without substance will be recharacterized: profits are allotted to a foreign permanent establishment or the controlling shareholder, DTA relief is denied, and the taxpayer faces reassessment, interest and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting PayPal and SWIFT sales from the die-cast model trade, issuing false invoices or fictitious purchase orders, suppressing inventory, or claiming private luxury spending as business expense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 175-176 DBG: fine equal to the tax evaded; where falsified documents are used, fiscal fraud is punishable by a fine up to three times the evaded tax and/or imprisonment up to 3 years; cantonal surcharges and default interest are cumulative.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any director who signs, prepares, or causes the submission of a knowingly false return is individually criminally liable; sanctions include prison, confiscation of personal assets, travel and banking restrictions, and the director may be required to make restitution of the tax loss.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Swiss AG as a paper vehicle with no physical presence or die-casting activity, delegating all management to a foreign parent, moving no business-related substance to Switzerland, and channelling intra-group profits solely to obtain Swiss treaty protection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss GAAR recharacterization and reassessment: foreign parent is treated as having a Swiss permanent establishment or the AG as transparent in whole or part; DTA benefits are denied; under-declared profit is taxed with interest; cannot liquidate without payment; additional penalties for incorrect return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly allow a sham structure can be sued by shareholders/creditors for damages under Art. 754 OR and Art. 41 CO; the Swiss court may pierce the corporate veil where assets and personal funds are commingled, leaving foreign directors subject to personal judgments and mutual legal assistance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation / Missing Local File
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling 1/18 scale die-cast models to a related Hong Kong distributor below arm's-length prices; paying brand royalties or management fees to the parent without a valid agreement, benchmark, or evidence of services; failing to prepare and submit Local File upon request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FTA upward adjustment of taxable income to the result that independent parties would obtain; additional federal/cantonal tax plus late-payment interest; administrative fine for incomplete documentation (commonly up to 30% of additional assessed tax); in serious cases treated as attempted tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving non-arm's-length pricing are personally liable to the company for damages caused by profit leakage; criminal exposure attaches if false contractual documents are created to justify the adjustment; foreign directors may be summoned and income/provisional measures taken abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying regular or hidden distributions (loan waivers, interest-free advances, unreasonably high bonuses, transfer of trade receivables below par) to non-resident shareholders without withholding and remitting 35% Swiss Verrechnungssteuer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FTA demands 35% WHT on the gross constructive dividend, plus default interest and procedural fine; failure to remit is a criminal offense; the amount due is secured by statutory first lien on the corporation's assets and can force insolvency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause or tolerate non-withholding are jointly and severally liable for the unremitted WHT where the AG is unable to pay; the FTA may pursue them personally, issue a payment order, and request exit restrictions for treating assets abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring incoming PayPal/SWIFT settlements into amounts below reporting thresholds, mixing personal and corporate accounts to conceal beneficial ownership, accepting third-party or 'nested' payments without understanding source of funds, and issuing false commercial invoices to launder sales proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of AMLA and related Swiss financial-penalty law carry imprisonment up to 3 years and fines up to CHF 500,000 for natural persons; for an entity, damage-causing fines and confiscation of all assets linked to the offense; the low-risk classification is withdrawn if such conduct appears.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable where they fail to take the necessary organizational measures when the AG's operations cross the financial-intermediary threshold or when they deliberately conceal suspicious payment flows; the Swiss courts may impose a professional ban, a travel ban, and extradition under mutual legal assistance.
